Tech Scan: Models

A coding task needs both a model that can do the work and a client that can reach it. Start with approved Claude and OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock; use the exceptions and typed-decision notes below when the task needs something different.

Draft research reference. Based on published documentation, not local deployment tests.

For the selection method, read Choose an AI model in Concepts.

On this page
Choose a model for the task AWS-first default Excluded from this route Gaps and open questions Sources

For model routing and tool access controls, see Tech Scan: AI gateway.

Choose a model for the task

First check that the required capability, data location and retention, identity, API, security boundaries and operational ownership fit the use case. Prefer AWS-managed services among options that pass those checks; AWS preference does not override them.

Fallbacks, retrieval reasoning and evaluator models need the same model approval as the primary call. Managed defaults and automatic routing cannot widen the approved list. Embedding and reranking models are approved separately from the generative models discussed here.

An inference profile names a model and the Regions its requests can route to. Amazon Bedrock offers system-defined cross-Region profiles and application profiles you create to track cost and usage for one model. Record the profile, not only the model name, when the route must stay inside approved Regions.[11]

Compare exact configurations on representative held-out tasks — tasks kept aside for assessment, not used to tune the model. Record correctness, correction effort, time, cost and control failures rather than choosing a model because it is newer.[2]

AWS-first default

Use approved Claude and OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock. Current official documentation includes frontier GPT models, not just GPT-OSS, and documents endpoint-specific API differences, so confirm the exact endpoint, region and features for the model you select.[1][3]

AWS-first default: models and coding clients
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Amazon Bedrock Model API for approved Claude and OpenAI models GA Default route for model access
Claude Code Coding client with documented Bedrock integration GA Default coding client through Bedrock
Codex Local coding client with documented Bedrock integration GA Default coding client through Bedrock

Claude Code and local Codex both have documented Bedrock integration.[5][4] Codex through Bedrock does not establish parity with Codex cloud or every hosted OpenAI feature; do not assume a feature available in the hosted service is available through Bedrock.

Managed GPT-OSS is an OpenAI model served through Bedrock, not self-hosted inference; it is not excluded merely by the provider rule.[3]

Before adopting the model, use the intended account to assess:

  • Representative task success
  • Required model and API support
  • Permission revocation
  • Timeouts and retries
  • Full cost

Conditional alternatives

Direct provider APIs are exceptions, not the assumed route. Use a direct Claude or OpenAI API only for a specific capability or an approved-region gap, after reviewing egress, credentials, retention and data handling. Compare the required feature with the documented Bedrock endpoint support before requesting the exception.[1]

Record the missing capability or region beside the exception, so the team can revisit it when Bedrock support changes.

Conditional alternatives to the Bedrock default
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Direct Claude API Provider API for Claude models GA Exception only: a specific capability or approved-region gap
Direct OpenAI API Provider API for OpenAI models GA Exception only: a specific capability or approved-region gap
OpenAI Decisions API Typed predicate, choice and score answers; model gpt-6-luna GA Conditional direct-OpenAI evaluation only
Claude Platform on AWS Claude access as a third-party offering on AWS GA Conditional feature route only

The OpenAI Decisions API is documented as generally available with gpt-6-luna and native predicate (yes/no), choice and score answers. No Box question is documented.[6][9] Treat it as a conditional direct-OpenAI evaluation. These checks are still required before any use:

  • Task accuracy
  • Calibration
  • Abstention and refusal handling
  • Application-side action checks

Bedrock support for /decisions is not established. Availability of the same model through Responses does not prove availability of that API.[7]

Claude Platform on AWS is a conditional feature route, not interchangeable compliance evidence for Bedrock. AWS identifies it as a third-party offering outside standard AWS compliance programmes.[8]

Research-only notes

A typed decision returns an answer in a fixed form that software can check. A fixed output shape does not establish accuracy or calibrated confidence. TypeSafe Jev, discussed as System One in Concepts, remains educational material rather than an approved deployment choice.[2]

TypeSafe's Box is opt-in and not production-ready. Jev itself is in public beta, not GA, and Box is a preview feature on top of that: neither the product's status nor the feature's status makes Box production-ready. The current documentation calls images and Box “Dreamer-ready” and requires the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true header; request formats, limits and accuracy can change.[10]

Choice, Score, Noul and Box are TypeSafe's question names, not a universal API vocabulary. The survey uses them to compare decision models:[9]

  • Choice: pick one option from a labelled set.
  • Score: place the input on an ordered scale.
  • Noul: TypeSafe's yes/no question; OpenAI uses predicate for its yes/no answer type, not a shared API contract.
  • Box: visual grounding, locating something in an image.
Explore other typed-decision candidates

The following records preserve the survey's comparison, not a second deployment shortlist. Its model descriptions and reported results have not been independently qualified here.[9]

Research-only typed-decision models
ProductWhat it isEvidence and maturityWhen to use it
TypeSafe Jev (System One) Hosted typed-decision model: Choice, Score, Noul, Box Launched 15 September 2026 in early access / public beta — no GA, no public SLA. Box arrived in Jev 1.14 (14 October 2026), 1.14-only, behind the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true header; preview, not production-ready. A Box answer is always a box (no “not found”), so pair a Box question with a Noul existence check and ignore the box when the Noul answer is low. Educational material only
Strands Decider 2B Open-weight typed-decision model: Choice, Score, Noul Survey and repository claims, not independent benchmark results Not recommended; removed from the approved-stack recommendation

Strands Decider 2B remains outside the recommendation. The survey describes Choice, Score and Noul, with no Box equivalent; its JevBench comparison draws on the repository's own table, not independent benchmark evidence.[9] Open weights or a permissive licence would not by themselves qualify it for this route.

The survey describes Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash as multimodal candidates with a vision encoder for images and video, hosted on Workers AI, but does not establish their Box support. Other research leads in the same survey are:[9]

  • Convai Laya
  • Liquid AI d1
  • Perplexity pplx-decider
  • Mapika decider-2b

These candidates remain outside the approved Claude/OpenAI route, not recommendations.

Excluded from this route

These exclusions describe this guide's stack, not the products' suitability elsewhere.

Excluded from the recommended route
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Self-hosted inference (vLLM, Ollama) Serves model weights on your own infrastructure Open-source projects (versioned releases) — no GA service Do not use on this route: no model-weight hosting infrastructure is needed, and self-hosting is a separate decision with its own qualification.
Amazon SageMaker fine-tuning and model import Fine-tunes or imports models on SageMaker GA Do not use until a concrete requirement exists
Nova, Llama and Mistral generative models Generative models outside the approved Claude and OpenAI policy GA Do not use on the recommended route

If the task needs self-hosted inference or a generative model outside Claude/OpenAI, raise that as a separate decision rather than assuming this route permits it.

Gaps and open questions

  • No suitable approved route for typed visual grounding is established here. TypeSafe documents Box, but it is experimental and outside the approved model route.[10] The reviewed OpenAI Decisions API documents no Box question.[6]
  • Bedrock support for /decisions is unresolved. Availability of the same model through Responses does not prove availability of that API.[7]
  • Claude Platform on AWS is not interchangeable compliance evidence for Bedrock. It is a third-party offering outside standard AWS compliance programmes, so a compliance case built on Bedrock cannot cite it.[8]
  • Model availability changes. A model listed today may later be retired or have its endpoint changed, so re-confirm the exact endpoint, region and features at adoption time rather than relying on this page's listing.[3]

To close the typed-decision gap, establish a production-ready, qualified Box model on an approved (Bedrock) route, or Bedrock support for /decisions, then assess it on the intended task. This gap does not mean approved multimodal models cannot locate objects; it concerns a suitable typed-decision interface, not visual grounding as a whole.

Next step: Record the chosen model, endpoint, task results and unresolved failures before adoption. Use the Harness reference to choose how the agent runs; existing approval and release authority still applies.
